exposure: bladder lesions located within 1 cm of the ureteral orifice
deeper invasive layer of lesions (mucosal layer)
outcome: urinary symptoms (urinary frequency, urgency, dysuria, hematuria)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 47 patients who were surgically confirmed to have bladder endometriosis at a tertiary referral hospital in China between January 2012 and December 2023.
finding: Previous cesarean section, dysmenorrhea, anterior compartment obliteration, lesion location, and depth of invasion were identified as factors associated with urinary symptoms in patients with bladder endometriosis, and while some achieved pregnancy after surgery, the independent effect on fertility was challenging to determine.
mod_finding: Previous cesarean section was significantly associated with the presence of urinary symptoms in patients with bladder endometriosis.
